name: Muiderpoort
description: The Muiderpoort is a surviving gate of Amsterdam’s former city wall. Cornelis Rauws designed the present classical gate after its predecessor collapsed in 1769; it was built in 1770–1771. Its two sculpted pediments show different city emblems: a medieval cog ship on the city side and the three Saint Andrew’s crosses on the outer side. Napoleon entered Amsterdam through this gate in 1811. The open passage retains a brick vault beneath the octagonal dome and clock lantern.
